added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own arm logs: baseline-arm.log at 4a5ec5081e records 58 passed with EXIT=0 and no FAILED line, and after-arm.log at c0ef2a0bb3 records 60 passed with EXIT=0 and no FAILED line, so the set difference is empty.

findings.text: the 50-pass band assertion is not a guard for this change, because the manifest and the fragment record that the base revision, which has no _release_pass_memory, also keeps 150 MiB to 152 MiB across the constant fixture, so reinstating the removal of the memory release leaves this assertion green and only the idle-reading case notices.

the assertion compares the reading's resident_bytes against a different call to service.resident_bytes(), the same function the code under test used, so both sides move together and a rewritten reader returning a constant stays true; the independent /proc helper the module already defines at line 28 is unused here, so the done_when's reading-to-/proc 10 % agreement is unmeasured.

_release_pass_memory calls file_memo.clear() unconditionally on every pass, while reckon/crew/admission/shared.py:222 and the fragment at line 16 say the memo is dropped only when the reading is above the bound, and clearing the process-wide parse memo every pass discards the cross-pass cache the memo exists to provide (reckon/file_memo.py:1), raising the read volume the plan's next section is trying to bound.

writing a reading for every idle pass puts a line carrying retired: [] immediately after one carrying a retirement, and reckon/crew/obligations.py:2170 recent_upstream_retirements returns only the last record's retired list, so a retirement is now readable for one pass instead of persisting through idle passes and a production consumer of this log silently loses it.
